MCP Activity

Turn a complete HTML, CSS and JavaScript experience into a Moodle activity that can be authored with ChatGPT or Claude (using the MCP protocol).

Teachers can build interactive lessons, simulations and assessments while Moodle remains responsible for activity visibility, question attempts and grades. Students use the published experience inside their course without needing an AI account.

What the activity supports
  • One HTML document with embedded styles and scripts.
  • Draft previews and explicit publication of immutable revisions.
  • Native question-bank questions and server-side answer validation.
  • Grades recorded through Moodle's native gradebook.
Interactive content with isolation
Custom JavaScript runs in a sandboxed iframe rather than inside Moodle's authenticated page, keeping the authored content separate from Moodle sessions and interfaces.
Questions stay in Moodle
Questions are stored in the native question bank before being linked to the activity. Answers are submitted to the server and evaluated by Moodle's Question Engine, not by browser-side scripts.
Controlled publication
New drafts do not replace the content learners are already viewing. Published revisions remain available until the teacher explicitly publishes an update.
When an activity needs more than static HTML

Embedding an interactive page is straightforward; making its assessments trustworthy is the harder part. MCP Activity keeps presentation in the authored document but leaves question versions, attempt state and grading to Moodle's established services, so learner scores do not depend on JavaScript running in the browser.

The activity integrates with local_mcp for AI-assisted authoring while keeping student access independent of ChatGPT or Claude. The current 0.1.0 alpha supports one attempt per learner, and its initial backup implementation does not restore student attempts. Assessment workflows should be validated before production use.
